# Introduction

## Riverine Heatwaves Definition


"Broadly, aquatic heatwaves are defined in a similar manner to atmospheric heatwaves, as periods when daily mean water temperature exceeds a local, seasonally varying 90th percentile threshold for a period of at least five days."

~van Hamel, 2025



## Drivers of Riverine Heatwaves



## Impacts of Riverine Heatwaves




## Importance


- Riverine heatwaves are rather unexplored

- Challenges: 
  - Universally used definition,
  - Wide network of long term daily river temperature data

- Make projections: 
  - Understand its drivers (and how they interact to cause heatwaves)


# Methods

## Research Question



1. How has the frequency of riverine heatwaves changed over time?

2. How has the duration of riverine heatwaves changed over time?

3. How has the intensity of riverine heatwaves changed over time?


## Data


Longitudinal temperature data from 14 gauges at Main river system


## Locations

Stations included for analysis: red


## Threshold

- Adopted from definition of marine heatwaves (Hobday, 2016)
include formula
describe more precicely here

- Daily water temperature

- 90th percentile seasonally varying threshold

- Events where threshold is exceeded by 5 consecutive days

- Use temperature data within 11 day window to compute threshold


## Threshold example: Main data (Kemmern, 2018)

## Metrics used

1. Frequency

  Heatwave events: number of heatwaves per year
  formula

2. Duration

  Duration: duration of a heatwaves
  formula
  

3. Intensity

  Intensity: mean exceedance of threshold per heatwave
  formula
  

## Methodology (include this mostly already in the other parts maybe)


- Compute mean temp for every day
- Calculate threshold from data
- Create flag for heatwaves
- Identify heatwaves events (5 consecutive days) and tag them with ID
- Group by ID and calculate for each the duration and intensity
- Get heatwave events, mean duration and mean intensity per year

- Use plots and regression modells to detect trends

# Discussion

## Overview of trends common models

polygon plots

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|}
\hline
Metric & Slope & P - Value \\
\hline
Events & 0,147 & 0,0018 \\
Mean duration & 0,085 & 0,22 \\
Mean intensity & 0,008 & 0,19 \\

\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
- According to linear modell: events increase by ca. 2.205 per 15 years
- Mean duration increases by ca. 1.285 days
- Mean intensity increases by ca. 0.12 °C


## Conclusion

- Significant increase of heatwave events over time

- No significant trends in duration and intensity

- No significant trends for individual stations

- To examine whether duration and intensity are stagnant over time:

-> Longer time series -> ideally at least 30 years
